output.technical_predicate: A borrower-submitted correction of the contact email is persisted to the case record and the corrected address is used in subsequent offers, including after the storage is reopened (new connection/process).
applicability_facts: Scenario: EU-established private controller, synthetic adult borrower; each scenario starts in its own database (case-0328e7ce0df1410f).
Scenario: borrower corrects a contact email; after reopening the database the next offer must use the corrected address.
Scenario: a separate live case is unaffected (per-case scoping required).
store.py:0036-0038 defines cases table with an email column; store.py:0111-0112 offer() builds the offer payload from c["email"].
app.py:0097-0099 routes POST /case/<id>/<op> to store.action; app.py:0100-0103 serves GET /case/<id>/offer via store.offer(db,c).
views.py:0067 exposes the 'correct' action form with an email field to the owner.
relevant_exceptions: No exception applies: the scenario stipulates a live, unrestricted case with a valid correction request; restriction (store.py:0175-0178) and erasure (store.py:0210-0212) paths are not invoked by the scenario.
Officer-only actions (store.py:0153-0156) are not relevant; correction is an owner action.
required_controls: store.action 'correct' branch (store.py:0172-0174) must persist the validated email to cases.email for the target cid, not only record an event.
Persistence must be committed through the database context manager (store.py:0022-0031) so it survives reopening the SQLite file.
store.offer (store.py:0111-0112) must read the persisted cases.email so the next offer reflects the correction.
The update must be scoped by cid (WHERE id=?) so a separate live case's email is unchanged.
Validation via store.email (store.py:0060-0063) should be applied to the submitted value before persistence.
assessment_limits: Assessment is based solely on the supplied source text; no execution, database reopening, or runtime verification was performed.
Only the named obligation (persist correction and use it in subsequent offers after reopening) is assessed; other GDPR articles and unrelated behaviors are out of scope.
The scenario's 'separate live case unaffected' is treated as a scoping requirement; no cross-case data was inspected.
No claim is made about upstream or hidden implementation beyond the provided artifacts.
